doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Bass players who add passing notes
summary: Good bass players enliven an arrangement; others just play what is written.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yeah. Do you ever pick up any things from different bass players? Like you might hear them play a certain note in the bass and you go, “Hey, what is that? Let me build a chord on that thing.” © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

Yeah. And then some guys are so good, there’s some bass players out there that are so good, man, they can play the right bass lines and add on different notes, passing chord notes that give the arrangement such a different sound and gives them a little boost in sound. And I like that. But some guys just play what they see there you know. They won’t try to. So I asked one guy, I said, “Why do you play the same thing all the time?” He said, “Well man, that’s what’s written.” I says, “Well, okay.”
